title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: MARISOL DRIVES
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Marisol Vega, a forty-four-year-old hotel housekeeper from Chicago.
She has ridden the L train for twenty-six years, and never once driven a car.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE PHONE CALL
segments.quote: Nothing in life is to be feared, it is only to be understood.
segments.author: Marie Curie
lines: Her daughter Gabby lives ninety miles away in Rockford, and her first baby was due in March.
No train goes there at three in the morning.
Then she remembered a poster from the scientist Marie Curie:
Nothing in life is to be feared, it is only to be understood.
So she signed up for driving lessons.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE EXPERT
segments.quote: It's what you learn after you know it all that counts.
segments.author: John Wooden
lines: Her teacher, Lyle Dunbar, was seventy-one, with a cardigan full of mints.
Marisol said, I've watched people drive for forty years. I know this.
Lyle smiled and quoted the basketball coach John Wooden:
It's what you learn after you know it all that counts.
Ten seconds later, she turned on the wipers instead of the blinker.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: LITTLE THINGS
segments.quote: It has long been an axiom of mine that the little things are infinitely the most important.
segments.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
lines: In week three, she nearly hit a man on a bicycle.
Lyle read her a line from Sherlock Holmes, by Arthur Conan Doyle:
It has long been an axiom of mine that the little things are infinitely the most important.
Mirror. Signal. Shoulder. Every single time.
Next week, the bicycle man waved. With all five fingers.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE ROAD TEST
segments.quote: There is only one thing that makes a dream impossible to achieve: the fear of failure.
segments.author: Paulo Coelho
lines: Then came the road test at the DMV. She hit the curb twice, and failed.
On the train home, she decided she just wasn't a driving person.
Gabby texted her a line from the Brazilian novelist Paulo Coelho:
There is only one thing that makes a dream impossible to achieve: the fear of failure.
She booked the next test that same night.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: TWO TRASH CANS
segments.quote: Perfection is not attainable, but if we chase perfection we can catch excellence.
segments.author: Vince Lombardi
lines: Every night, she practiced parking between two trash cans in the alley.
The neighbors brought lawn chairs. One man sold popcorn.
Lyle quoted the football coach Vince Lombardi:
Perfection is not attainable, but if we chase perfection we can catch excellence.
On test day, the examiner just said, huh. She passed.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THREE A.M.
segments.quote: A mother's love for her child is like nothing else in the world.
segments.author: Agatha Christie
lines: In March, at three in the morning, the phone rang. The baby was coming.
It was pouring rain, and her hands were shaking on the wheel.
She thought of a line from the mystery writer Agatha Christie:
A mother's love for her child is like nothing else in the world.
Ninety miles later, she was holding her new granddaughter, Luz.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Understand fear. Keep learning. Mind the little things. Try again. Chase better. Go for love.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Understand your fear. Keep learning. Mind the little things. Try again. Chase better. Go for love.
Me, I drive like my grandfather. Both hands, and the blinker on since nineteen ninety.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
